paper.title_en: $D^{(*)}Δ$ interactions and the molecular interpretation of $Σ_c(3200)^0$
paper.abstract_en: Inspired by the recent observation of the $Σ_c(3200)^0$ baryon in the $Λ_c^+π^-$ invariant mass spectrum by the LHCb Collaboration, we perform a comprehensive investigation of the $D^{(*)}Δ$ interactions within the one-boson-exchange framework. Our results show that the $D^*Δ$ molecule with $I(J^P)=1(1/2^-)$ can be regarded as the most natural candidate for the $Σ_c(3200)$, and predict the existence of several $D^*Δ$ molecular partners with $I(J^P)=1(3/2^-, 5/2^-)$ and $2(1/2^{\pm}, 3/2^{\pm}, 5/2^-)$. After including the coupled channel effects between $DΔ$ and $D^*Δ$, several shallowly bound $DΔ$-dominated molecular candidates also emerge, especially for the $I(J^P)=1,2(3/2^-)$ and the $2(1/2^+,3/2^+)$ systems. These results provide a unified molecular interpretation of the newly observed $Σ_c(3200)^0$ and useful guidance for future experimental searches for exotic charmed-baryon states. We expect the high-statistics data from the LHCb Upgrade and Belle~II runs will directly test these predictions.
